member.name: T:NaturalGasPipeline.Hydraulics.AgaTransmissionFactorModel
member.summary:
AGA transmission factor (AGA NB-13 method, as presented by Menon, Gas Pipeline Hydraulics), covering both turbulent zones:
partially turbulent (smooth-pipe law with drag factor Df): Ft = 4·log10(Re / Ft) − 0.6 F = 4·Df·log10(Re / (1.4125·Ft)) fully turbulent (rough-pipe law): F = 4·log10(3.7·D/ε) F = min(partially turbulent, fully turbulent), f (Darcy) = 4 / F².
With Df = 1 the partially turbulent value equals Ft (4·log10 1.4125 = 0.59995): Ft reproduces the AGA table printed by Arnold & Stewart, Figure 6.16 (e.g. 22.028 at Re = 10⁷), see tests.
The drag factor accounts for bends and fittings (bend index); typical values 0.90–0.99. It is an explicit input: there is no default. Laminar and transitional flow (Re < 4000) are outside the method.

member.name: T:NaturalGasPipeline.Hydraulics.FlowRegimeFrictionModel
member.summary:
Base for correlations that only describe turbulent flow.
Regime handling, shared by every derived model: - Re < 2300: laminar, f = 64 / Re (exact, Hagen–Poiseuille); - 2300 ≤ Re < 4000: transitional, the friction factor is not defined by these correlations → (use if the transition must be crossed); - Re ≥ 4000: the derived turbulent correlation.
The 2300 laminar limit is the usual one for pipe flow (e.g. Çengel & Cimbala); Arnold & Stewart use 2000. Both bracket the same unstable band.

member.name: T:NaturalGasPipeline.Hydraulics.ColebrookWhiteModel
member.summary: Colebrook–White (1939), implicit: 1/√f = −2·log10( (ε/D)/3.7 + 2.51 / (Re·√f) ) Solved by fixed-point iteration from a Swamee–Jain start (|Δf| < 1e-12). The reference turbulent law for commercial pipe; the Moody chart is a plot of it. Verified against the exact Lambert-W solution to better than 1e-11.

member.name: T:NaturalGasPipeline.Hydraulics.HaalandModel
member.summary: Haaland (1983), explicit: 1/√f = −1.8·log10( ((ε/D)/3.7)^1.11 + 6.9/Re ) Validated range: 4·10³ ≤ Re ≤ 10⁸, ε/D ≤ 0.05. Measured maximum |deviation| from Colebrook over that range: 1.42 %.

member.name: T:NaturalGasPipeline.Hydraulics.SwameeJainModel
member.summary: Swamee & Jain (1976), explicit: f = 0.25 / [ log10( (ε/D)/3.7 + 5.74/Re^0.9 ) ]² Validated range: 5·10³ ≤ Re ≤ 10⁸, 10⁻⁶ ≤ ε/D ≤ 10⁻². Measured deviation from Colebrook over that range: up to +2.83 % (largest at Re = 5·10³, ε/D = 10⁻²; well below 1 % for transmission lines).

member.name: T:NaturalGasPipeline.Hydraulics.ChurchillModel
member.summary: Churchill (1977), single explicit equation for ALL regimes (laminar, transitional and turbulent): f = 8 · [ (8/Re)¹² + (A + B)^(−3/2) ]^(1/12) A = [ 2.457 · ln( 1 / ((7/Re)^0.9 + 0.27·ε/D) ) ]¹⁶ B = (37530 / Re)¹⁶ Reduces exactly to 64/Re in laminar flow and is continuous through the transition, so an iterative solver never stops there. Measured deviation from Colebrook (4·10³ ≤ Re ≤ 10⁸, ε/D ≤ 0.05): up to +3.11 %, near the low-Re / high-roughness corner. In the transition band the value is an interpolation, not a measured law.

member.name: T:NaturalGasPipeline.Hydraulics.AgaFullyTurbulentModel
member.summary: AGA fully turbulent (rough-pipe) law, as used in the AGA equation: F = 4·log10( 3.7·D/ε ), f = 4 / F² Independent of Re; valid above the critical Reynolds number where the AGA partially-turbulent (smooth-pipe) transmission factor meets it: Re_c = 3.7·10^0.15 · (D/ε) · F ≈ 20.9 · (D/ε) · log10(3.7·D/ε) (Arnold & Stewart print the constant as "20,912"; it must be 20.912 — with it their Example 6.7 gives Re_c = 9.03·10⁵, as stated.) Requires ε > 0.

member.name: T:NaturalGasPipeline.Hydraulics.GasVelocityCalculator
member.summary:
Gas velocity and the API RP 14E erosional velocity.
Mean velocity from mass flow: V = ṁ / (ρ·A), A = π·D²/4. With ṁ fixed, V ∝ 1/ρ ∝ Z/P, so in a pipe section the highest velocity is at the lowest pressure (station suction or delivery point).
Erosional velocity, API RP 14E as given by Arnold & Stewart, Surface Production Operations (2016), Eq. 6.15: V_e = C / √ρ with V_e in ft/s and ρ in lbm/ft³, C = 100 continuous service, 125 intermittent, 60 corrosive. Converted exactly to SI here: V_e[m/s] = C·0.3048·√(16.018463)/√ρ[kg/m³] ≈ 1.2199·C/√ρ. RP 14E was written for production-facility piping and is generally regarded as conservative for clean, dry transmission gas; its use as a pipeline limit is a design choice, not a code requirement.

member.name: T:NaturalGasPipeline.Hydraulics.IsothermalGasFlowSolver
member.summary:
Steady, isothermal, single-phase gas flow in one pipe segment with a uniform slope. This is the General Flow Equation written in SI with the Darcy friction factor:
P1² − e^s · P2² = f · G² · a · L / D · (e^s − 1) / s
G = ṁ / A mass flux, kg/(m²·s) a = Z·R·T / M (≈ squared isothermal sound speed), m²/s² s = 2·g·Δz / a elevation parameter (s → 0: (e^s − 1)/s → 1)
Derived by integrating dp/dx = −ρ·g·sinθ − f·ρ·v²/(2D) with ρ = P/a.
Assumptions (none of them silent; each is stated here): - isothermal flow at the given temperature; - Z, μ and therefore Re and f evaluated at the average pressure P_avg = 2/3·(P1 + P2 − P1·P2/(P1 + P2)) and held constant; - kinetic-energy (acceleration) term neglected; - constant slope over the segment (split long profiles into segments).
Verified against direct numerical integration of the differential equation with local Z(p): 0.02 % of ΔP for a flat 50 km line and 0.35 % with 500 m of climb (see IsothermalGasFlowSolverTests).

member.name: T:System.Runtime.CompilerServices.ModuleInitializerAttribute
member.summary: Used to indicate to the compiler that a method should be called in its containing module's initializer.
member.remarks:
When one or more valid methods with this attribute are found in a compilation, the compiler will emit a module initializer which calls each of the attributed methods.
Certain requirements are imposed on any method targeted with this attribute: - The method must be `static`. - The method must be an ordinary member method, as opposed to a property accessor, constructor, local function, etc. - The method must be parameterless. - The method must return `void`. - The method must not be generic or be contained in a generic type. - The method's effective accessibility must be `internal` or `public`.
The specification for module initializers in the .NET runtime can be found here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/design/specs/Ecma-335-Augments.md#module-initializer

member.remarks:
The diagnostic ID is shown in build output for warnings and errors.
This property represents the unique ID that can be used to suppress the warnings or errors, if needed.

member.name: P:System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExperimentalAttribute.UrlFormat
member.summary: Gets or sets the URL for corresponding documentation. The API accepts a format string instead of an actual URL, creating a generic URL that includes the diagnostic ID.
member.value: The format string that represents a URL to corresponding documentation.

member.name: T:System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ConstantExpectedAttribute
member.summary: Indicates that the specified method parameter expects a constant.
member.remarks: This can be used to inform tooling that a constant should be used as an argument for the annotated parameter.

member.name: P:System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ConstantExpectedAttribute.Min
member.summary: Indicates the minimum bound of the expected constant, inclusive.

member.name: P:System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ConstantExpectedAttribute.Max
member.summary: Indicates the maximum bound of the expected constant, inclusive.
